analysis_steps.goal: Fit parameterized 1D disk model to visibilities

method.value: Isothermal slab model of 13C18O, C18O and dust inside the snowline, with Keplerian field; model cubes sampled at observed uv points and compared in visibility space

evidence.quote: we carry out Fourier transforms on the model image cubes and retrieve the complex visibilities at the ($u,v$)-plane locations sampled by the ALMA observations

evidence.quote: We fix $v_{\rm turb}$ at 0.01 km s$^{-1}$

evidence.quote: The abundance ratio of C$^{18}$O/$^{13}$C$^{18}$O is assumed to be constant throughout the disk and modeled as a free parameter(cite: Miotello14).

claims.experiment: Visibility-space MCMC fit of 1D disk model

evidence.quote: We report the first direct measurement of the mid-plane CO snowline at 20.5$\pm1.3$ AU, in the TW Hya disk.

claims.finding: MMSN/MMEN should not be used as quantitative templates

evidence.quote: should not be used as quantitative templates of initial mass distribution for planet formation models.

why_this_data.value: 13C18O and C18O are far less abundant, so probe the mid-plane deeper

evidence.quote: Their optical depths are correspondingly much smaller than the $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO lines, and thus can probe much deeper regions in protoplanetary disks.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gas surface density jump from dust-based models (Models 2 and 3) rejected

evidence.loc: CO snowline or jump in gas surface density.
evidence.quote: We find that neither models based on dust observations (Model 2 and 3) could reproduce the observed C$^{18}$O emissions.

limitations_admitted.value: Dust opacity uncertainty from grain growth not included
